prompt:
Create one 15-second horizontal 16:9 cinematic video block. Follow the exact shot timing below; total duration is 15 seconds.

CONTINUITY FROM PREVIOUS BLOCK:
Jamshid has reached the mount area. Zahhak continues upward toward the unchanged Hall of Columns and throne.

SHOT 1 — UNCHANGED HALL — 0:00–0:04:
24mm restrained frontal wide shot in the exact existing Hall of Columns. Zahhak enters at one horizontal edge and advances toward the unchanged throne on the central axis, completing one heavy gait cycle. No followers enter. Cut on the staff striking the first throne step.

SHOT 2 — MOUNT KNEELS — 0:04–0:08:
Match the impact to the enormous two-legged flightless mount lowering beside Jamshid. 35mm side view. The 2.5-to-3-meter terrestrial animal is heavy and plausible, with massive legs, weighty beak or muzzle, coarse feathers and areas of skin. It has no usable wings, never flies and never resembles Simurgh, griffin or hippogriff. It bends until the functional saddle reaches Jamshid. He swings on in one practical movement and leans forward; no climb or pose.

SHOT 3 — NEW OCCUPANT — 0:08–0:11:
50mm centered frontal view of the exact unchanged Jamshid throne. Zahhak lowers himself using the staff to control his lame side, plants it and becomes still. No crown and no victorious head lift. One serpent crosses the throne arm while another turns toward the empty hall.

SHOT 4 — SMALL IN THE LAND — 0:11–0:15:
Extreme wide static 24mm horizontal desert landscape. Jamshid and the mount run away along descending ground, already small in the lower third. Heavy terrestrial two-legged strides only; no leap, glide or flight. Dry wind softens their track as they become one moving dark point. Cut to black before complete disappearance.

GLOBAL EXECUTION RULES:
Horizontal cinematic frame, exact 16:9 aspect ratio. Never crop or compose vertically. Use the full horizontal width for architecture, lateral blocking, negative space and opposing movement. Every uploaded reference is an immutable identity or design anchor. No redesign, no identity merging and no transfer of masks or costumes. All imagery is physically real, tactile and grounded. No dialogue, narration, music, titles or readable text. No heroic fantasy montage, no glossy commercial light, no magic, no smoke, no floating particles, no drone spectacle, no orbit, no speed ramp and no slow motion. Iranian crowd masks have smooth continuous human-like surfaces and small eye openings; never skull, skeletal, Mexican or Day-of-the-Dead masks. Zahhak is exactly 178 cm, permanently lame and visibly dependent on a staff whenever standing or walking. His five to ten natural black serpents remain alive and move independently across shoulders, neck, back and upper torso; never static ornaments, never dragons and never a Medusa arrangement.

SOUND:
Staff on throne step, heavy animal joints and harness leather, strained breath, cloth and serpent scales as Zahhak sits, then open desert wind and receding two-legged footfalls. Wind is the last sound; cut to silence.
